item.title: Dense ideals in forcing extensions of Nairian models
item.description: arXiv:2611.28226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complementing the work of Blue, Larson, and Sargsyan~\cite{NM,NM2}, we obtain forcing extensions of minimal Nairian models in which the Axiom of Choice and the Generalized Continuum Hypothesis hold. In these extensions, every uncountable regular cardinal $\kappa$ carries a precipitous, uniform, $\kappa$-dense ideal $\mathcal{I}_\kappa$. In fact, $\mathcal P(\kappa)/\mathcal{I}_\kappa$ is isomorphic to the regular open algebra of $\textrm{Col}(\omega,\kappa)$. This extends Woodin's theorem on the existence of $\omega_1$-dense ideals on $\omega_1$ in forcing extensions of models of $\Theta_{\rm reg}$ \cite[Section~2.3]{ASTWZ24}, where $\Theta_{\rm reg}$ denotes the theory $\textrm{ZF}+\textrm{AD}_{\mathbb R}+\text{``$\Theta$ is regular''}$. Moreover, our work places the consistency strength of the aforementioned theory on generic embeddings below a Woodin cardinal that is a limit of Woodin cardinals, and also complements the seminal work of Eskew and Hayut~\cite{EH24}.
item.dc:creator: Rahman Mohammadpour, Grigor Sargsyan

item.title: A Note on the Topos-Inadmissibility of Free Heyting Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.28247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Yiqi Xu and Linguan Ye have recently settled the long-standing open question about which Heyting algebras are topos-admissible, that is, occur as the truth values of some topos. They prove that free Heyting algebras with two or more generators are not topos admissible. Their proof has been simplified by Zoltan Kocsis and by Sam van Gool. Here I make some further simplifications, emphasising algebraic methods over Kripke semantics and in particular the use of Sierpi\'nski cones of Heyting algebras.
item.dc:creator: Andrew M Pitts

item.title: Taming Fitch's and Humberstone's Paradoxes
item.description: arXiv:2611.29149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fitch's Paradox says that if every true proposition is knowable, then every true proposition is known. Humberstone's Paradox states that if every true proposition is known by at least one of a set of finitely many agents, then some agent in that set knows every true proposition. Both paradoxes give rise to surprising and unacceptable consequences. In this paper, we diagnose a crucial tacit presupposition underlying these paradoxes, namely that the domain of propositions is closed under Boolean operations such as intersection and union, and offer a uniform resolution. We argue that the paradoxical inferences rely implicitly on this closure assumption. By adopting weak propositionally quantified modal logics that drop these closure conditions, we provide a semantically motivated account that blocks both paradoxes. The restriction on universal instantiation is not an ad hoc technical device, but reflects a conception of propositions as graspable objects of epistemic attitudes, on which the domain of propositions need not be closed under Boolean operations, since some Boolean combinations of graspable propositions may not themselves be graspable.
item.dc:creator: Jie Fan

item.title: A logic of strong contingency
item.description: arXiv:2611.29182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, inspired by the notions of contingency and strong possibility, we propose a notion which may be called 'strong contingency'. This notion can be seen as a mixture of contingency and strong possibility. We investigate the logic with strong contingency as a sole primitive modality, including its bisimulation notion, expressivity, frame definability, and axiomatizations. It turns out that this logic is expressively incomparable with the standard modal logic and the logic of contingency even over the class of S5-models, and less expressive than the logic of strong possibility and weak necessity over the class of S5-models. Besides, as the introduction of the inequality into the semantics makes the completeness proof much harder, instead of showing the completeness via a canonical model construction, we reduce the soundness and strong completeness of the involved proof systems to those of the existing proof systems in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Jie Fan

item.title: $\Sigma^1_3$ Gandy-Harrington Forcing
item.description: arXiv:2611.29432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gandy-Harrington forcing is an important tool in descriptive set theory, first developed by Gandy and later used by Harrington to give a simple proof of Silver's dichotomy theorem. In this paper, we develop a new version of Gandy-Harrington forcing higher up in the projective hierarchy, under an appropriate local determinacy hypothesis. Using this new forcing, we prove a reverse mathematics result at the level of $\Delta^1_2$-Determinacy as well as new inner-model-theoretic basis theorem for $\Sigma^1_3$ sets.
item.dc:creator: William Chan, Sandra M\"uller, Farmer Schlutzenberg, Benjamin Siskind

item.title: The cardinal invariants of the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff null ideal are independent of $s$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $0 < s < 1$, let $\mathcal{N}^s$ denote the ideal of sets of $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure zero. We prove that $\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{N}^s) = \operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{N}^t)$ and $\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{N}^s) = \operatorname{non}(\mathcal{N}^t)$ for all $0 < s, t < 1$. The proof uses Ren and Wang's solution of the Furstenberg set conjecture. This answers open questions of Shelah--Stepr\=ans and Elekes--Stepr\=ans.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Goto

item.title: On the uniformity of definably amenable radicals and dfg-fsg decompositions in $p$-adically closed fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.29554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For definable families of groups over $p$-adically closed fields, we show that the definably amenable radicals and their dfg-fsg decompositions can be defined uniformly as the prime $p$ and the family parameters vary.
item.dc:creator: Zhentao Zhang

item.title: $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property
item.description: arXiv:2611.30227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(E, P)$, $(E', P')$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{C}$ with marked $p$-torsion points; a marked isogeny is an isogeny sending $P$ to $P'$. We show the marked isogeny relation is interpretable in $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and has strict infinite chains. It follows that $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property, which confirms a special case of the stable fields conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Spencer Dembner, Cole Franklin

item.title: Equivalence of Cohen generics is hyperfinite
item.description: arXiv:2611.30679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that the equivalence relation on Cohen generic reals over a countable model of set theory, where two are equivalent if they produce the same generic extension, is hyperfinite, answering a question of the author. The proof uses asymptotic separation and is a digestion of an argument originally produced by GPT-6.
item.dc:creator: Iian B. Smythe

item.title: On Cohen Generic Sets in Supercompact Prikry Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\kappa$ be $\lambda$-supercompact for a regular $\lambda>\kappa$. We show that if $\lambda$ is not the successor of a singular of cofinality below $\kappa$, $\diamondsuit(S^\lambda_{\geq\kappa})$ implies that every ${<}\kappa$-strategically closed forcing of size at most $\lambda$ is a projection of the $\lambda$-supercompact Prikry forcing. We show that the situation for successors of singulars of small cofinality is independent. Finally, we provide more limitations about the class of $\kappa$-distributive projections of the $\lambda$-supercompact Prikry forcing and give examples of $\kappa$-distributive forcings of size $\lambda$ which cannot be projections of this forcing.
item.dc:creator: Tom Benhamou, Gabriel Goldberg

item.title: Computability of states and non-computability of traces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28337v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study computable presentations of the state space and trace space of computably presented C*-algebras. We show that the state space has a computably compact presentation with respect to which the evaluation of states is a computable map. As an application of having computable states, we obtain a computable version of the GNS construction. We show that the trace space does not share these computational properties. Specifically, we give an example of a computable presentation of a simple AF algebra for which the trace space has no computably compact presentation with respect to which evaluation is computable. As a consequence, we demonstrate that the Elliott invariant of a computably presentable classifiable C*-algebra is not always presentable in a way that makes all key features of the invariant computable.
item.dc:creator: Christopher J. Eagle

item.title: $\mathsf{Y} \& \mathsf{X}$: Intermediate Logics of Convex Hulls and Cross-Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.29298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate two logics of geometric Kripke frames: $\mathsf{Y}$, defined by finite convex hulls, and $\mathsf{X}$, defined by cross-polytopes. We characterize the validity of the Kreisel--Putnam axiom on convex hull frames by means of convex independence. Our main technical results concern several reductions obtained using two translations, $C$ and $D$. In particular, we show that $\mathsf{X}$ is invariant under $C$, while $\mathsf{Y}$ is invariant under $D$. Moreover, the same translation $D$ reduces Medvedev logic to every logic in the interval $[\mathsf{Y}',\mathsf{Med}]$, where $\mathsf{Y}'$ is a naturally defined intermediate logic strictly between $\mathsf{Y}$ and $\mathsf{Med}$. Together with geometric arguments, these reductions establish that $\mathsf{Y}$, $\mathsf{X}$, and $\mathsf{Cheq}$ are pairwise incomparable, while each lies strictly between $\mathsf{PL}$ and Medvedev logic. We also prove that every logic in $[\mathsf{Y},\mathsf{Med}]$ is not finitely axiomatizable and that this interval contains continuum many distinct logics. In addition, every logic in $[\mathsf{Y}',\mathsf{Med}]$ is undecidable. We prove that $\mathsf{X}$ is undecidable and $\mathsf{Y}\in \Pi^0_1$. In particular, we show that it is decidable whether a finite poset is isomorphic to a finite convex hull frame, and that the logics determined by configurations of a bounded number of points are decidable. Finally, we extend our study to infinite convex hull frames. We show that inclusion yields $\mathsf{KC}$, whereas reverse inclusion yields $\mathsf{IPC}$. For the latter result, we use the Cantor set to construct $p$-morphisms onto arbitrary finite rooted frames.
item.dc:creator: Yumin Ji, Han Xiao

item.title: Turing Completeness of Greedy UNO with an Ultimately Periodic Infinite Deck
item.description: arXiv:2611.29739v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We encode an arbitrary two-counter Minsky machine as a two-player UNO round with an ultimately periodic infinite draw pile $uw^\omega$. The construction uses a fixed $17$-card prefix and a period of length quadratic in the number of instructions. When both players follow the same fixed greedy policy, the round terminates exactly when the machine halts, and every available hand play has a unique card type. Consequently, greedy termination and victory by a designated player -- as well as winning-strategy existence under forced-play rules without tie-breaking -- are $\Sigma^0_1$-complete. Under official voluntary-draw rules with unrestricted legal choices, however, the existence of a finite play is decidable (and primitive recursive) via reachability in fixed-dimension vector addition systems with states (VASS). Finally, the maximal duration of a finite greedy play has no total computable upper bound in the input length.
item.dc:creator: T. V. Kuptsov (Lomonosov Moscow State University), G. A. Khaziev (Institute for Information Transmission Problems RAS, Central University)

item.title: Tableau Consequence under Positive Contexts: A Reconstruction of Walukiewicz's Completeness Proof
item.description: arXiv:2611.30009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a positive-context lifting theorem for tableau consequence in the modal $\mu$-calculus: under explicit syntactic hypotheses, $\mathcal T_B\Rightarrow\mathcal T_C$ induces $\mathcal T_{A(B)}\Rightarrow\mathcal T_{A(C)}$. The proof orders instances of the given relation by birth time and assigns overlapping formula occurrences to the oldest supporting instance. A corollary gives bidirectional replacement by automaton normal form inside positive contexts. Together with a separate unfolding consequence lemma and ANF bisimulation, the lifting theorem yields a self-contained reconstruction of Walukiewicz's completeness proof for Kozen's axiomatisation and makes its least-fixpoint step more transparent. We also give a finite parity-game proof of regular-refutation existence and a two-sided transfer from tableau consequence to thin refutations.
item.dc:creator: Kuniaki Tamura

item.title: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
item.description: arXiv:2611.30644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the Andr\'e-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Pila

item.title: Diophantine sets over global function fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.31218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $q\equiv 3\bmod 4$ be a prime power and let $K$ be a finite separable extension of the field of rational functions $\mathbb F_q(t)$, with constant field $\mathbb F_q$. We show that $\mathbb F_q[t]$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb F_q(t)$ and that the latter is Diophantine in $K$. We deduce from work of Demeyer that $K$ has the DPRM property: Diophantine sets over $K$ are the same as listable sets.
item.dc:creator: Hector Pasten, Xavier Vidaux

item.title: Double negation stable h-propositions in cubical sets
item.description: arXiv:2209.15035v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a construction of classifiers for double negation stable h-propositions in a variety of cubical set models of homotopy type theory and cubical type theory. This is used to give some relative consistency results: classifiers for double negation stable propositions exist in cubical sets whenever they exist in the metatheory; the Dedekind real numbers can be added to homotopy type theory without changing the consistency strength; we construct a model of homotopy type theory with extended Church's thesis, which states that all partial functions with double negation stable domain are computable.
item.dc:creator: Andrew W. Swan

item.title: Extremely amenable automorphism groups of countable structures
item.description: arXiv:2411.02760v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study the isomorphism relation of extremely amenable non-Archimedean Polish groups from the point of view of descriptive set theory. Our main result is that this relation is more complex than any isomorphism relation of countable structures in the Borel reducibility hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Su Gao, Feng Li, Ruiwen Li

item.title: Comeager hereditary families of compact sets are big
item.description: arXiv:2608.13523v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a Polish space and let $\mathcal K(X)$ be its Vietoris hyperspace. A family $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal K(X)$ is hereditary if it is downward closed under inclusion. Matheron and Zelen\'y asked whether every comeager hereditary family in $\mathcal K(X)$ contains a dense hereditary $G_\delta$ subfamily. We give an affirmative answer in ZFC.
item.dc:creator: Peter Ban\'a\v{s}

item.title: Equivalence of Restricted and Full Division
item.description: arXiv:2610.24976v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$ that the restricted Euclidean division principle $\mathrm{pa17}^{-}$, which asserts division only for co-prime pairs, is equivalent to the full principle $\mathrm{pa17}$. The proof uses a transformation that preserves the quotient in division with remainder to reduce an arbitrary division problem to one for a co-prime pair. This answers Visser's Open Question 8.29 and shows that the restricted principle has the same strength as full Euclidean division over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$. An appendix further shows that $\mathrm{PA}^{-}_{\mathrm{jer}}+\mathrm{pa17}$ proves both the predecessor principle $\mathrm{pa14}$ and the subtraction principle $\mathrm{pa15}$.
item.dc:creator: Naoya Kato

item.title: Finite refutations in countably additive quantum probability
item.description: arXiv:2611.05656v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We axiomatize countably additive quantum probability and prove a completeness theorem for finite refutation beyond compactness: inconsistency is witnessed by refutations each of whose branches ends in finitely many jointly unsatisfiable commitments. Adjoining the hypothesis that every event has a predetermined, context-independent outcome makes the theory inconsistent, although every finite subset of the resulting axioms has a model. For a countable theory of closed bounds on sentence values in our real-valued infinitary logic, inconsistency is equivalent to a winning strategy for a challenger in a game against a model builder. The challenger chooses each test in response to the builder's commitments, and the plays that follow a winning strategy form such a refutation. For the quantum theory with predetermined outcomes, every winning strategy must branch infinitely at some node. In the strategy we construct, countable additivity locates the four-dimensional subspace in which a finite Kochen-Specker parity argument applies. In their standard models, our axioms describe the closed subspaces and the density-operator probabilities of a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. We prove in ZFC that the sets of probability values definable uniformly across standard models are exactly the $\sigma$-projective subsets of the unit interval.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Aubone, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: A true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
item.description: arXiv:2611.07321v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehat{\phi}$ denotes its interpretation on $\omega$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehat{\phi}$ is a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Golshani

item.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
item.description: arXiv:2611.21390v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.
item.dc:creator: Monroe Eskew, Curial Gallart

item.title: Alain Badiou's Mistake: Two Postulates of Dialectical Materialism
item.description: arXiv:1301.1203v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Originally published in 2013, this revised article constitutes the first stage of a two-part intervention that revisits Alain Badiou's deployment of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. It interrogates the structural and philosophical consequences of taking the category-theoretic foundations of mathematics seriously, extending the formal boundaries of mathematical discourse. This part focuses on Logics of Worlds, which emerged as Badiou's response to his own theory of subjectivity. While revisiting structures implicit in his reading of Cohen's proof of the independence of the continuum hypothesis, I demonstrate how his concept of 'dialectical materialism' remains constrained by set-theoretic ontology and localic topos theory - essentially a theory of intuitionistic logic. In particular, Badiou's claim that categorical thinking does not substantially change mathematics overlooks the true geometric momentum driving topos theory. While the primary contents of this article are technical, I further explore how Badiou's formal omissions critically impact his philosophical project. This is especially visible in regard to his 'postulate of materialism' - a device he utilizes to promote dialectical materialism as a credible alternative to science. Through its category-theoretic reframing, I show that the postulate actually encapsulates two structurally different conditions, one of which directly constrains his own project while the other part captures a type of atomism juxtaposed with Badiou's condescending assessment of democracy. By leveraging such claims indebted to his pre-committed, logicist comprehension of mathematics, Badiou reinstitutes an absolutist Truth-doctrine and an ultimately despotic political program against a genuine concept of multiplicity. His errors thus hardly constitute merely an inadvertent formal slip, but indicate a deeper, political intent.
item.dc:creator: Antti Veilahti

item.title: Complexity as Axiomatic Incompleteness
item.description: arXiv:2408.10211v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: IInformation theory has long sought to uncover the universal laws governing complex systems. Yet information is not merely quantified; it is also interpreted by observers.We formalize this cognitive aspect through a Generalized Incompleteness Theory (GIC), which integrates axiomatic logic, Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, and G\"odel's incompleteness theorem to establish a connection between complexity and formal incompleteness. We introduce the notions of interpreter-based information and PAC complexity, demonstrating that certain outputs can be PAC-learnable even when their corresponding interpreters cannot be constructed. We further show that every nontrivial formal system contains a PAC-learnable incompleteness space of dimension \(2^n-n-1\). The GIC framework unifies several foundational results-including Cantor's diagonal argument, G\"odel's incompleteness theorem, and the Turing halting problem-within a categorical and topological framework. We further show that physical models, including four-dimensional spacetime in relativity and the 11- and 26-dimensional spaces arising in string theory, admit natural correspondences with incompleteness spaces, while critical states can be understood in terms of symmetry-breaking selections of axioms. Our framework identifies incompleteness as a universal feature underlying complexity, criticality, and observability, thereby revealing fundamental limits on description and cognition in any axiomatizable theory.
item.dc:creator: Zhifeng Ma, Zhangang Han

item.title: The Solver's Paradox for SAT
item.description: arXiv:2511.14665v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show in Rocq that every circuit verifier $v$ determines a formula $\psi_v$ whose satisfiability is $v$'s acceptance of its own diagonal claim: a satisfiability predicate thus behaves like a provability predicate. Every solver represented in the language misclassifies its own diagonal instance, and every verifier misjudges its own diagonal claim. We distinguish our result from (i) the refuters of Chen et al. (2024), which produce from the description of a solver an instance it gets wrong, and (ii) the refuter of Gutfreund et al. (2007) for efficient SAT solvers, which needs a hardness hypothesis and a simulation. Here the refuter is purely syntactic, and it separates evaluation of the language from its own expressions, not SAT from a resource-bounded class. The identity behind the fixed point uses no property of quotation; its reading as self-reference depends on the coding, and an injective recoding flips the branch. A truth table decides $\psi_v$ only from outside the language. Written inside, it is brute force: it settles the claim from above and has a diagonal instance of its own. This yields an unconditional certification hierarchy with tower growth, a quadratic lower bound on every internal evaluator, and an exponential lower bound on brute force.
item.dc:creator: Milan Rosko

item.title: G\"odel-Tarski Translation for Constructive Logics with Transitive Closure
item.description: arXiv:2603.05131v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the semantically-defined constructive propositional dynamic logics of regular programs $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$, respectively extending the basic constructive modal logic $\sf CK$ and its Wijesekera-style variant $\sf WK$. Using translations between our logics and $\sf PDL$, we show that both $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$ are {\sc ExpTime}-complete and enjoy an exponential-size finite model property. In particular, their diamond-free fragment, restricted to a single atomic program and its reflexive transitive closure is already {\sc ExpTime}-complete, thereby settling the conjecture of Afshari et al. By embedding $\sf CS4$ and $\sf WS4$ into our logics, we show their validity problems are also in {\sc ExpTime}, improving the previously known {\sc NExpTime} upper bound obtained via finite model arguments.
item.dc:creator: Sof\'ia Santiago-Fern\'andez, David Fern\'andez-Duque, Joost J. Joosten

item.title: Fuss-free cumulative universes: theory and practice
item.description: arXiv:2607.11329v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Universes are central to dependent type theory, and they are notoriously difficult to handle in a way that is both correct and usable. We propose a new "fuss-free" generalised algebraic presentation for polymorphic cumulative universes that dispenses with the intricate theory of coherent universe coercions in favour of a simpler formulation, which we prove equivalent by means of a normalisation theorem for the former. We study the fuss-free formulation by means of (1) an abstract specification of its bidirectional elaboration algorithm, and (2) a concrete implementation in Haskell. We also describe and implement an extension of the fuss-free universe hierarchy with a judgemental notion of datatype description from which prior notions of cumulative inductive type may be derived.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Sterbac, Jonathan Sterling

item.title: What Can Postselection on Halting Decide?
item.description: arXiv:2611.20517v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A probabilistic program can produce an answer on some runs and continue forever on others. Suppose it halts with positive probability on every input and we count only the runs that halt. Aaronson et al. showed that if the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one, such programs decide exactly the problems solvable with a finite list of halting questions chosen in advance. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be more likely than the wrong one. We prove that the resulting class is exactly $\boldsymbol{\Delta^0_2}$: the halting questions can now be asked one at a time, with each answer helping to determine the next question. This remains true if the program must halt with probability at least 99%, or with any other prescribed rational lower bound below one. Our main technical result is the exact query bound when the program gives two guarantees. Suppose it halts with probability at least $\rho$ and, among the runs that halt, the correct answer has probability at least $a$. For rational $0 < \rho < 1$ and $1/2 < a < 1$, these programs decide exactly the problems solvable with at most $n$ halting questions chosen in advance, where $n$ is the largest integer satisfying $\rho(a/(1-a))^n \le 1$. Every value of $n$ occurs, and different values give different classes. The proof measures how much additional halting probability a change of answer requires, and counts these changes as in Ershov's hierarchy. The results extend to quantum machines with computable gates.
item.dc:creator: Saman Farhat, Farzad Didehvar

item.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over quadratic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.25002v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic fields $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2),\mathbb Q(\sqrt3),\mathbb Q(\sqrt6)$. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ with $d\in\{2,3,6\}$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{24}\in K$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun
